title: Decide whether to wire the opum-lore eval suite into CI now that claude plugin eval is GA
description:
`claude plugin eval` went generally available 2026-09-11 in Claude Code 2.1.269+ (docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals). The locally installed CLI is already 2.1.269, so the tooling is in reach today.

CURRENT STATE, checked rather than assumed:
- This repo carries an eval suite for the opum-lore plugin at evals/ — two cases, lore-doc-request (graders: skill-fired, outcome) and lore-no-trigger (graders: skill-fired, criteria).
- NOTHING runs it. No .github/workflows/ job invokes it; the only 'eval' hits in release.yml are an unrelated report gate. No package.json script runs it either.
- The single committed result set is evals/results/2026-09-05T06-09-10-658Z/. So the last recorded run predates the skill being federated from a tag.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY: skills/lore/SKILL.md is federated to the opum-lore marketplace entry from a git tag (see LCLI-469). opum-marketplace's check-federated-content.mjs asserts the skill's BYTES match a baseline — it cannot assert the skill still TRIGGERS correctly. A skill can stay byte-stable and still regress in behaviour when the model underneath moves, and conversely a deliberate skill edit ships to every federated consumer with no behavioural gate anywhere in the chain. The eval suite is the only thing in this repo that tests the triggering behaviour, and it currently runs only when a human remembers to.

THE DOCUMENTED CI SHAPE (from the GA page, per opum-agent): --trust-plugin, --json <path>, --max-cost-usd, pinned --model and --judge-model, exit codes 0/1/2/130/143.

THE CAVEAT THAT DECIDES THE SHAPE: a run that hits a plan usage limit scores 0 WITHOUT the suite being marked partial. That is a false red that is indistinguishable from a genuine regression. It rules out making this a required status check until there is a way to tell the two apart — a required check that goes red on someone else's usage limit wedges the ref for reasons unrelated to the change under review.

RECOMMENDED SHAPE IF ADOPTED: scheduled (not per-PR) and non-blocking, with --max-cost-usd set and both --model and --judge-model pinned so a model rollout is a deliberate bump rather than a surprise red. Per-PR is the wrong trigger twice over: it spends money on every unrelated docs change, and the skill it tests changes rarely.

THIS IS A SPEND DECISION, so it goes to the user rather than being adopted on a peer's fact. Nothing is blocked by leaving it manual.

Side observation worth recording: the 2026-09-10 history rebuild means there is no longer any way to tell from git when skills/lore/SKILL.md last changed relative to that 2026-09-05 eval run — the whole history is one root commit. Any future 'is the eval stale relative to the skill' check has to be built on content hashes, not on commit dates.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision is recorded: wire the eval suite into CI on a schedule, or leave it manual — with the reason, so a future session does not re-open it fresh
If adopted, the job is non-blocking and scheduled rather than per-PR, with --max-cost-usd set and --model/--judge-model pinned
If adopted, the usage-limit-scores-0 caveat is handled or explicitly accepted in writing, since it is indistinguishable from a real regression
If left manual, that is stated where someone editing skills/lore/SKILL.md will see it, since federation ships the skill with no behavioural gate

implementationNotes:
SHAPE SETTLED 2026-09-11, only the spend decision remains.

The orchestrator has recorded the recommended shape in the fleet doc as THE CI form for a plugin eval suite: scheduled rather than per-PR, non-blocking, --max-cost-usd set, and both --model and --judge-model pinned. Whoever picks this up does not need to re-derive or re-argue the shape — it is settled fleet-wide. Exactly one thing is still open: whether this repo spends money on scheduled eval runs. That is the user's call.

The generalisation behind this task was also adopted as an estate-audit check rather than a one-time question to each repo: for every plugin-carrying repository, report an eval suite that no workflow or script runs, and compare the newest committed result against the SKILL'S CONTENT HASH rather than commit dates — the latter being meaningless here since the 2026-09-10 rebuild collapsed the history to a single root commit.

Consequence: the audit will surface this repo every time it runs, until the decision is recorded either way. Deciding 'leave it manual' and writing that down is therefore a real outcome, not a deferral — it stops the finding recurring. Do not close this by wiring something up merely to silence an audit line.
